questions.question: Dr Sami Kikou and Dr Mina Lilou receive a patient for the extraction of tooth 46. Sami, confident, grabs his elevator. Mina asks him: 'Are you sure you want to start with that?' Sami replies: 'Of course, a simple extraction is defined as:'
options: An extraction without tooth sectioning or bone surgery
An extraction with osteotomy and flap
An extraction of a complex impacted tooth
questions.explanation: Sami is right! A simple extraction is done with an elevator and forceps, without bone surgery. Mina, assisting him, adds: 'For once he's right, I'll give him the benefit of the doubt!'

questions.question: Mina assists Sami during an extraction. She hands him the instrument to luxate the tooth. Sami takes it and says: 'Perfect, as usual!' Mina retorts: 'You never make mistakes?' The elevator is used to:
options: Luxate the tooth before extraction with forceps
Extract the tooth directly without forceps
Section the tooth into several fragments
questions.explanation: Mina explains to the student: 'The elevator is used to luxate the tooth.' Sami adds: 'And next time, try not to break the bone table!'

questions.question: Sami must extract a maxillary incisor. Mina, who knows his habits, hands him the forceps he always uses. It is:
questions.explanation: Mina hands him the N° 1 forceps. 'Always the same, you're so predictable Sami!' she says. 'Why change when you've found perfection?' he retorts.

questions.question: Mina must extract a maxillary molar. Sami, assisting her, hands her the specific forceps:
questions.explanation: Sami hands her the N° 18 forceps. 'You see, I know my forceps too!' Mina replies: 'Yes, but do you know how to use them?'

questions.question: Mrs. Khadija, a loyal patient, returns 3 days after an extraction. Sami diagnoses a dry socket. Mina, who examines her afterwards, confirms it. Mina explains to the patient that a dry socket is:
options: A painful inflammation of the post-extraction socket
An acute bacterial infection of the maxillary bone
Persistent bleeding due to the absence of a clot
A fracture of the vestibular bone table
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Dry socket is caused by the loss of the clot.' Sami adds: 'And if you had smoked, Khadija, I would have told you!'

questions.question: Sami and Mina argue about the main risk factor for dry socket. Sami claims it is smoking. Mina asks him: 'Are you sure about that?'
options: Yes, smoking is the main risk factor
No, it is the patient's gender
questions.explanation: Sami is right, even if it's thanks to an article Mina had sent him. 'I told you so, Mina!' he exclaims.

questions.question: Mina, with great rigor, treats Mrs. Khadija's dry socket. Sami, assisting her, observes and comments: 'You see, I taught you how to do it right!' Treatment begins with:
options: Gentle irrigation and a sedative socket dressing
questions.explanation: Mina performs gentle irrigation and places a sedative dressing. Sami, teasing, says: 'You see, I taught you everything.' Mina replies: 'Yes, but I do it better!'

questions.question: Sami explains to a patient that an impacted wisdom tooth is a tooth that has not erupted normally. Mina, next to him, adds: 'And if you listen to Sami, he'll repeat it five times.'
options: A tooth that has not erupted normally
A tooth fractured at the apical level
A decayed tooth with pulp necrosis
questions.explanation: Sami is right: the mandibular wisdom tooth is the most frequently impacted. Mina confirms while teasing him.

questions.question: Mina receives an asymptomatic patient with an impacted wisdom tooth. She explains that the recommended management is:
options: Extraction or monitoring depending on age
questions.explanation: Mina presents the two options. Sami intervenes: 'I would have extracted directly.' Mina: 'That's why I'm the most competent.'

questions.question: During an impacted wisdom tooth extraction, Sami and Mina agree on the most serious complication. Sami: 'The inferior alveolar nerve!' Mina: 'I agree, for once.'
options: Injury to the inferior alveolar nerve
questions.explanation: Both agree: the inferior alveolar nerve is at risk. A rare moment of concord followed by another jab: 'You see Sami, we can agree!'

questions.question: Mina, always precise, explains to a trainee that osteotomy consists of sectioning the bone around the tooth. Sami intervenes: 'Sectioning, that's the word I use when I cut cheese.'
options: Sectioning the bone around the tooth
Extracting the tooth without a flap
Suturing the edges of a flap
questions.explanation: Mina is firm: osteotomy consists of cutting the bone. Sami, teasing, adds: 'And I do it with the elevator, it's faster!'

questions.question: Sami performs an odontectomy in front of a trainee. He explains that this technique consists of sectioning the tooth into several fragments. Mina, assisting him, adds: 'And the more you section, the more chances you have of missing a fragment.'
options: Sectioning the tooth into several fragments
Extracting the tooth in one piece
questions.explanation: Sami sections the tooth to facilitate extraction. Mina, assisting him, ensures that no fragment is forgotten.

questions.question: Mina, who leaves nothing to chance, asks her assistant for the instrument to section a tooth. Sami, next to her, suggests: 'An elevator, like me!' Mina: 'No, a surgical bur.'
questions.explanation: Mina uses the bone or dental bur for sectioning. Sami, observing her, admits: 'Okay, it's more precise.'

questions.question: During a maxillary molar extraction, Sami suspects an oroantral communication. He explains to Mina that it is:
options: A perforation between the sinus and the mouth
A fracture of the maxillary tuberosity
questions.explanation: Sami is right: it is a possible complication. Mina, assisting him, says: 'You're lucky I'm here to fix your mistakes!'

questions.question: Mina finds a small OAC of less than 2mm. She decides to monitor and protect the clot. Sami: 'I would have sutured!' Mina: 'That's why you do more sutures than me!'
questions.explanation: A small OAC can heal spontaneously. Sami, a little annoyed, admits: 'Okay, you're right.'

questions.question: Sami is called for a large OAC of more than 4mm. He decides to close with a repair flap. Mina, assisting him, says: 'You see, you know how to do it when you take your time!'
questions.explanation: Sami performs the surgical closure with the precision inspired by Mina's presence.

questions.question: Mina performs a flap to access an impacted tooth. Sami, assisting her, asks: 'Do you want me to show you how it's done?' Mina: 'No thanks, I've already seen your flaps.'
options: A gingival flap to access the bone
questions.explanation: Mina explains that the flap allows surgical access. Sami, teasing, adds: 'And I'm faster without a flap.' 'And less precise!' she retorts.

questions.question: Sami shows a trainee the common types of flaps. He emphasizes the envelope or triangular flap. Mina, next to him, intervenes: 'You're forgetting the semi-lunar flap?'
questions.explanation: Sami presents the basic flaps. Mina adds: 'And the semi-lunar, do you know it?' 'I know it, but I don't use it, it's too long!'

questions.question: Mina sutures a flap after a complex extraction. Sami, observing her, says: 'You always do too many stitches!' Mina: 'Better too many than not enough.'
questions.explanation: Mina sutures carefully. Sami, assisting her, comments on each stitch, which makes her smile.

questions.question: Sami uses resorbable sutures to save time. He explains to his patient that this avoids removal. Mina, next to him, intervenes: 'Yes, but non-resorbable sutures are safer.'
questions.explanation: Sami defends his resorbable sutures. Mina, assisting him, reminds him that she prefers non-resorbable ones.

questions.question: Mrs. Khadija returns with persistent bleeding. Sami diagnoses a post-extraction hemorrhage. Mina, consulted in second opinion, confirms. Sami: 'You see, we agree!'
options: An infection of the soft tissues
questions.explanation: Both agree on the diagnosis. Sami adds: 'I'll let you handle it, you're better at sutures.'

questions.question: Mina treats the persistent hemorrhage with compression, hemostatic agent and suture. Sami, assisting her, says: 'You see, if I had been there, I would have done the same.'
questions.explanation: Mina follows her methodical protocol. Sami, assisting her, says: 'I do the same.' 'No, you do compression-suture and you forget the hemostatic agent!'

questions.question: Sami receives a patient with an uncontrolled acute infection. He knows it's a contraindication to extraction. Mina, next to him, adds: 'Finally you think before you act!'
questions.explanation: Sami knows that sometimes the infection must be treated first. Mina, assisting him, says: 'You're making progress!'

questions.question: Mina prescribes antibiotic prophylaxis to a patient at risk of infective endocarditis. Sami: 'You're too cautious!' Mina: 'And you're too reckless.'
questions.explanation: Mina strictly follows the guidelines. Sami, assisting her, admits: 'Okay, you're right for once.'

questions.question: Sami prescribes the first-line antibiotic. Mina, assisting him, asks: 'Are you sure?' Sami: 'Amoxicillin 2g, as always!'
questions.explanation: Sami prescribes amoxicillin. Mina, assisting him, reminds him: 'Don't forget penicillin allergy!'

questions.question: Mina reminds her trainee that any surgical procedure must be preceded by informed consent. Sami, next to her, adds: 'She's right, but I do it in 30 seconds!'
options: The opinion of the prosthetic laboratory
questions.explanation: Mina is strict about consent. Sami, assisting her, says: 'You're too slow, I've already done it.' 'Not well enough, that's why I check!'
